findings.quote: Red light has a wavelength of $600$ nm in vacuum.
findings.problem: 600 nm light is not red in standard color tables. Common bands put orange at about 590 to 620 nm and red from about 620 nm up; HyperPhysics lists 600 nm as yellow, with orange at 630 nm and red at 665 nm. A student who learns '600 nm is red' can choose red on a wavelength-to-color item. Color edges are approximate, but no standard source I found puts 600 nm in red. The calculation itself (2.00e8 m/s, 400 nm, 5.0e14 Hz) is correct and does not depend on the color word. This sentence was added in the rewrite; the base had no wavelength value.
findings.source: HyperPhysics, Spectral Colors (hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/specol.html), accessed 2026-11-04; common visible-spectrum band tables (orange 590 to 620 nm, red 620 to 750 nm); checklist B01
